sections: 13. What DISL still lacks for this type

items.reason: Tab as a second key of Add child is the host's keyboard convention (XMind's), which it maps onto the entry's one shortcut, Insert; a context tool states one shortcut, as DISL's entries do.

hostCode.behaviour: A new node is named from its siblings: one past the highest number of the numbered stem most of them share, else `New` and a last word at least two share, else `Node`, made unique ignoring case.
Add child and Add sibling create the node at once under the sibling name, a child as the last child and a sibling right after the node, then ask for its text in place.
Add child runs on any node; Add sibling is refused on the central topic.
Deleting a leaf goes without asking; deleting a branch asks first, with the words of the specification's deletion confirmation.
Collapsing and expanding is the viewer's own state: nothing is written and nothing lands on the history.
Notes are edited in a prompt and written as one edit.
Link to offers the project's files and folders, skipping `.git`, `node_modules`, `bin`, `obj` and `.claude`, and Unlink removes the link.

The central topic is centred on the origin, its first-level branches split to its right and left as their POSITION says or alternately from the right, each list of siblings a column centred on its parent, with gaps of at least 10 and 48 growing to a tenth of the wider box; collapsed branches take no room.
A node is measured with a 14 font at 0.55 per UTF-16 code unit and a 1.4 line, padded 10 and 6, at least 32 wide, rounded to two decimals.
A body is a map only when it is well-formed XML whose element is `<map>` holding exactly one `<node>`; a carriage return is kept as written, so a Windows save comes back byte for byte.

A node's id is its `ID`, its text its `TEXT` or the plain text of a `richcontent TYPE="NODE"`, its notes the plain text of a `richcontent TYPE="NOTE"`, its link `LINK`, its folded flag `FOLDED`, its side `POSITION`.
A new map is a `<map>` holding one central topic named after the file.
Every `<node>` is read as a Node with its parent and place; a later holder of an id the file gives twice is read under an ephemeral id and keeps what the file writes as `storedId`.
A map's findings are its specification's constraints over what the reader read, a body that is not a map giving only `mindmap.not-a-map`, and a duplicate id named by what the file writes.
Folding a branch writes `FOLDED` into the file as an undoable edit, and a rename stamps `MODIFIED`.
